clue.text: 2000 guards like going round Black Sea spa seeking morbid type of pleasure

indicators.note: the Roman numeral pair guards, holding inside it, everything that follows

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000, so two of them make 2000

indicators.note: going round means the little word is wrapped around the resort's name

parts.note: like in the sense of 'as' (sing like a bird, sing as a bird does)
Sochi is a resort city on Russia's Black Sea coast

explanation.surface: Someone seeking an odd kind of enjoyment goes round a Black Sea resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'going round' acts on the inner pair first, making ASOCHIS, then 'guards' sets that between the Ms; 'seeking' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the taking of pleasure from one's own pain or humiliation, a morbid kind of gratification.

clue.text: Michael nurses a very stunted stray animal

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, so the name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Mick is short for Michael

indicators.note: stunted means cut short, so the last letter of very is removed

explanation.surface: A man called Michael cares for a small lost creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbranded calf that has strayed from the herd, the original sense of the word.

clue.text: Please speak without shaking fist

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb goes around the other letters

parts.note: say, to utter

indicators.note: shaking means the letters of fist are jumbled

explanation.surface: A polite request to talk without waving a clenched hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like the polite word; it is the verb to gratify.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to gratify or content them.

clue.text: Company accountant leaves

parts.note: a CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A firm's accountant quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departing; it is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried foliage of a South American shrub, chewed as a stimulant.

clue.text: Getting off to a late start spoils cricket session

indicators.text: Getting off to a late start
indicators.note: a late start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: winnings, the spoils of a contest

explanation.surface: A late start ruins a cricket session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a verb meaning ruins; it is the noun for prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A batting turn in cricket, the period one side spends at the crease.

clue.text: More adult game about to be curbed by Etonian's mum

indicators.note: curbed by means held in by, so the turned game sits inside

parts.note: mater, Latin for mother, is old public-school slang; Eton is a famous English boarding school

indicators.note: about means the letters for the game are turned round

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A grown-up game is restrained by a public schoolboy's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning grown-up, so further developed.

clue.text: Large numbers returned in aircraft

indicators.note: returned means the word for large numbers is read backwards

parts.note: lots, as in 'lots of people'

explanation.surface: Many planes came back to base.
explanation.definitionFit: Short take-off and landing craft, an aviation abbreviation for a type of plane.

clue.text: US singer-songwriter formulated limits for Lasker-Noether theorem

indicators.note: formulated means the letters are put into a new form, rearranged
limits for means the outer letters of the hyphenated name

explanation.surface: An American musician devised a mathematical theorem.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting surface: he was a Harvard mathematician as well as a satirical songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Harvard maths lecturer was famous for witty satirical songs at the piano.

clue.text: See 7
I peter out after performing revolutionary dance?

indicators.note: performing means the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dancer runs out of steam after a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics; it means spinning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet spin on one foot, so a whirling, revolving move.

clue.text: See the author loading two containers

indicators.note: the containers are loaded with, so hold inside them, the writer's pronoun

parts.note: a vat and a can are both containers
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Look at the writer filling a couple of tubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a verb here but a bishop's seat; the Holy See is the papal jurisdiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's seat of government, is based in this city-state.

clue.text: Leader of Israel contributed to President Bush's ultimate victory

indicators.note: the leader of Israel is contributed into, so placed inside, the president's name

parts.note: Donald Trump, US President when the puzzle appeared

indicators.note: leader of means take the first letter of Israel
ultimate means the final letter of Bush's

explanation.surface: An Israeli leader helped a US president to a win.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great win or success.

clue.text: What's in Paris? Eiffel Tower

indicators.note: What's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: What do you find in the French capital? The Eiffel Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' reads as the noun after Eiffel, but it is the verb: to tower is to soar up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tower is to soar or ascend high, as a peak does over the land.

clue.text: Unexpected reactions to drug

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of reactions come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A medicine has produced surprising side effects.
explanation.definitionFit: To drug someone is to put them into a stupor with a narcotic.

clue.text: Cashier blowing top in fury

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the first letter

parts.note: to cashier is to dismiss, to fire

explanation.surface: A till worker loses their temper in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a person at a till; it is the verb to dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger or wrath, a synonym of rage.

clue.text: Newspaper guy

definitions.meaning: to guy is to mock or tease someone

explanation.surface: A man who works for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are slang: a tabloid paper, and to make fun of someone.

clue.text: Tramp fills lots of paper bottles

indicators.note: the vagrant fills, sits inside, the paper

parts.note: reams, bundles of 500 sheets
hobo, a vagrant

explanation.surface: A vagrant stuffs heaps of paper into bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Big wine bottles holding six standard bottles' worth, named for a king of Israel.

clue.text: Partner of Bonnie Scotland's runner

definitions.meaning: Bonnie Parker's criminal partner was ... Barrow
a runner is a river; this one flows through Glasgow

explanation.surface: The companion of a pretty lass is a Scottish athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonnie' looks like Scots for pretty; it is the outlaw Bonnie Parker.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw Barrow ran with Bonnie Parker, and the Glasgow river is a famous Scottish waterway.

clue.text: Spelling expert corrected errors checking compliance with English

indicators.note: checking in the sense of holding back, so the rearranged letters hold the other two inside
corrected means the letters of errors are put right, into a new order

parts.note: C abbreviates compliance

explanation.surface: An expert speller fixes mistakes to keep within English rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' looks like orthography; it means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is expert in casting spells, so is a spelling expert.

clue.text: About to screen Oliver Stone film about President Grant

indicators.note: to screen means to hide behind, so the film's title sits inside

parts.note: on, as in a book on a subject
W. is Oliver Stone's 2008 film about President George W. Bush

explanation.surface: A film director plans to show a biopic of the Civil War general turned president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Grant' looks like one name; 'President' belongs to the wordplay and 'Grant' is the verb to admit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to concede or admit it.

clue.text: Blend of Irish drinks bottled by Catholic church

indicators.note: bottled by means held inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
O, the Irish surname prefix as in O'Brien
ales, beers

explanation.surface: A mix of Irish beers kept in a Catholic church.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together and merge into one, as a mixture does.

clue.text: Working at fair wearing skimpy skirt, or something even skimpier

indicators.note: the skirt is worn around the other pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: a miniskirt, a mini
on, as a machine is on
OK, middling or acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone at a fair in a tiny skirt, or wearing even less.
explanation.definitionFit: A topless swimsuit, just the bottom half of a bikini, so briefer than a miniskirt.

clue.text: Agreement in parts of Louisiana

indicators.note: in parts of means the answer is found within the state's name

explanation.surface: A deal is accepted in some regions of a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting surface: French is still spoken in parts of Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for yes, an expression of assent.

clue.text: Follow in the footsteps of Italian visiting India and China

parts.note: I is India in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so Italian goes inside the friend

parts.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate)

explanation.surface: Trace another's route by touring Italy, India and China.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone's behaviour, as if walking where they walked.

clue.text: Current Republican Party entertains torture for US punk singer

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: entertains means takes in as a guest, so the party holds the other word

parts.note: the GOP, the Grand Old Party
gyp, pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: The modern Republicans enjoy torment, says an American rocker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage name of James Osterberg, the American punk-rock frontman.

clue.text: Dance beat at grand ball

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
O looks like a ball

explanation.surface: A dance takes place at a grand ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: A robin flies around island capital

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters sit around the island letter
flies means the letters flit into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden bird flits round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Rose also, having gone for gym instruction, moved faster

indicators.note: having gone for means one piece leaves and another replaces it

parts.note: stood up, rose to one's feet
too, also
PE, physical education

explanation.surface: Someone rose too and went to the gym to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Accelerated, went more quickly.

clue.text: Move to the right alternatives for energy, in hindsight

indicators.note: in hindsight means looking back, so the picked letters are read in reverse
alternatives for means take every other letter of energy

explanation.surface: Turning right to look for other sources of power, with hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is the call to a horse to turn to the right.

clue.text: Various opinions on government killing?

indicators.note: on means the next piece comes after, written on the end
various means the letters of opinions come in a different order

explanation.surface: People hold differing views about the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that killing is only one outcome of this.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder by administering a toxic substance is one form of killing.

clue.text: Some of the upper crust is backing a Liberal

indicators.note: backing means the little word is turned round

explanation.surface: Some aristocrats are supporting a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper crust' looks like the upper classes; it is the geological crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists name the upper layer of the earth's crust, rich in silica and aluminium, with this word.

clue.text: Seaweed extract found in a 32

parts.note: the answer to 32 down, a fish

explanation.surface: An extract from seaweed is found in a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly from red algae, used in labs and cooking.

clue.text: Old character in love with a married postgraduate

parts.note: dig is slang for to like or love
an MA is a master's degree, a postgraduate qualification

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person is smitten with a married graduate student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person; it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete letter of the early Greek alphabet, so an old character.

clue.text: Fish 15A hauled up

indicators.note: hauled up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the answer to 15 across, a newspaper

explanation.surface: A fish is pulled out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A garfish, a long-snouted fish.

clue.text: High-flyers succeeded at business

indicators.note: at shows the abbreviation sits at the end

parts.note: as in 'not my pigeon', meaning not my concern or business
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Successful people did well in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyers' suggests achievers; here they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds fly high, so are literal high-flyers.

clue.text: Korean explorer

definitions.meaning: Mungo ... was the Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: An adventurer from Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: A very common Korean family name, and the surname of Mungo, who explored West Africa.

clue.text: Old forward is back in style, showing adroitness

parts.note: ex means former, so old
pert means cheeky or forward

indicators.note: back in means the final letter of style

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned forward is back in fashion and shows skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' looks like a reversal of is; 'back in' picks the last letter of style.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill and know-how, the quality of being adept at something.
